Cc: Jordan Park <jordan@acme-analytics.com>

Subject: Canary fallback playbook + QBR exec asks

Thanks team — quick recap from this morning's cross‑functional sync and a proposed set of exec asks to surface during QBR prep. Attaching the initial canary playbook (PDF) and a draft QBR ask spreadsheet.

High level: we need agreement on fallback thresholds and the decision path for when a canary should be rolled back vs throttled to dedicated capacity. This is a QBR‑level ask because it impacts SLA exceptions and customer communications.

Action items (proposed owners / deadlines):
- Agree fallback thresholds (p50/p90 error rate delta, 10m rolling) — owner: Vivek — due Wed 7/21 EOD
- Confirm canary percentage ramp plan and max duration — owner: Karthik — due Tue 7/20 noon
- Prepare customer communication template for impacted customers — owner: Marissa — due Wed 7/21 noon
- Validate compatibility with Acme Analytics integration (Jordan looped) — owner: Jonas — ongoing

Notes / rationale:
- We should prefer automatic fallback to the nearest compatible model variant when latency increases but reserve manual rollback for correctness regressions.
- For QBR: call out estimated cost delta for an automatic fallback path (Optimize recommendations + margin). See sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1qBrQBR-ASKS

Attachments: canary-playbook-v1.pdf, qbr-ask-spreadsheet.xlsx

Jonas Weber
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Canary fallback playbook + QBR exec asks

Thanks Jonas — looks good. Two clarifying asks:
1) When you say "p50/p90 error rate delta" can we make that concrete? Propose: p50 increase > 2x or p90 increase > 1.5x relative to baseline for 10m rolling window triggers a fallback.
2) Canary duration: recommend 2h steady state (after ramp) as the default, with a 24h max for slow signals.

If that works I'll lock the exec ask text and add the SLA exception language.

Thanks for looping me in — Acme has a scheduled integration test next week (7/26). Quick notes from our side:
- We rely on session affinity for long‑running inference jobs; automatic fallback to a smaller model would break affinity unless you preserve KV state. Can we confirm the fallback path preserves session cookies/KV?
- If the fallback introduces a 20% latency increase, our cost model changes; we need a heads up window and a clear rollback timeline.

We can run a compatibility pass during your canary window if you want — happy to coordinate.

— Jordan Park
Integration Lead, Acme Analytics

Cc: Jordan Park <jordan@acme-analytics.com>

Subject: Re: Canary fallback playbook + QBR exec asks

Thanks. Technical responses / proposals:
- Agree with Karthik's concrete thresholds. I'll implement the 10m rolling window checks for p50/p90 and add a secondary signal for token‑generation failure rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m.
- Fallback behavior: we can preserve KV cache for sessions by shimming a KV migration path between model variants — that'll add a ~200ms overhead but keep semantics. Recommend that be the default for customer‑facing fallbacks; for internal canaries we can skip KV preservation to speed rollback.
- Canary ramp: propose 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 30m windows, steady for 2h, max duration 24h. If error signal observed at any step, immediate throttle back to previous step and notify owners.

Snippet of config I'll use (high level):
- check_window: 10m
- p50_trigger: 2.0x
- p90_trigger: 1.5x
- failure_rate_trigger: 0.5%
- canary_ramp: [1,5,20]
- steady_state: 2h
- max_duration: 24h

I'll push a PR to the playbook repo and attach a short runbook for oncall.

Vivek Kulkarni
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turns — finalizing exec ask language below for QBR deck and locking owners/dates.

Executive ask (one paragraph):
We request approval for a standardized canary fallback playbook that enables automatic, policy‑driven fallbacks to compatible model variants to preserve service availability. Approval includes: (1) adoption of the specified thresholds (p50 2x / p90 1.5x over 10m rolling), (2) default canary ramp and duration (1%→5%→20%, steady 2h, max 24h), and (3) allowance for KV‑preserving fallbacks for customer‑facing traffic with a small latency overhead. The estimated incremental cost impact is captured in the attached QBR asks sheet.

Locked owners and deliverables:
- Vivek: PR + runbook for canary checks, implement triggers — due Wed 7/21 EOD
- Karthik: finalize exec slide text and SLA exception phrasing — due Tue 7/20 noon (completed)
- Marissa: customer comms + QBR one‑slide — due Wed 7/21 noon
- Jonas: coordinate Acme compatibility pass and confirm integration window (7/26) — ongoing

Related links: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/canary-playbook, https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1qBrQBR-ASKS, HubSpot deal RED-8392.

If there are no objections I'll put the exec ask into the QBR deck by EOD and email leadership the ask with the one‑slide summary.

Jonas Weber
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
